pages.api:
# API

> Stdout is one report object, then an optional SenML array. The export is GET-only on loopback.

## Report

`schema` is `weavelogic.cog-output.v0`. `cog` is `ld6004-radar`. `timestamp` is Unix seconds. `sensor_class` is `radar`.

`source.kind` is `ld6004-uart`. `source.verified` is true only when checksum-valid frames arrived and the run was not `--simulate`. `source.simulated` is true for `--simulate`.

`health` is `ok`, `degraded`, or `no_source`. `quality` is null when `health` is `no_source`.

`frame` is `radar_local`. `axes` names that frame: X lateral, Y toward the bottom edge of the board, Z forward out of the antenna. `camera_above_radar_m` is 0.30, the bench camera height. It is not subtracted from X. `targets` is the `0x0A04` list for this window (empty means none arrived). Each item has `x_m`, `y_m`, `z_m`, `above_radar_m` (`-y_m`), `dop_idx`, `cluster_id`. There is no `velocity_m_s`. `dop_idx` is the protocol's integer; its unit is not stated. `points` is the `0x0A08` list, with the same height field. `zones` is null until a zone frame arrives, then four values of true, false, or null.

`vitals` is the string `not_defined`. The JSON has no heart-rate field and no breathing-rate field.

`writes` is `none` or `query-firmware`. `foreign_firmware` is true after a project code other than 0 or 6.

## SenML

When the window contains module status, the next stdout line is one JSON array. Every record has `bn` (the source id with a trailing slash), `n`, `v`, and `proof_`. `proof_` is `MEASURED` for UART bytes and `SYNTHETIC` for `--simulate`.

`hold_delay` uses SenML unit `s`. `z_min` and `z_max` use `m`. `sleep_period` is milliseconds and has no SenML unit, so `u` is omitted. `stay_life`, `output_interval`, and the enum fields also omit `u`.

Person positions and zone occupancy are not SenML.

## Export

Bound to `127.0.0.1:8055` by default. `GET` only.

| Path | Body |
|---|---|
| `/` | A short index |
| `/status` | The latest report |
| `/senml` | The latest pack, or `[]` |
| `/guide` | `{"toml","pages"}` for this cog version |
| `/spatial` | NDJSON, only in a `spatial-evidence` build, and only for lines produced with `--spatial-out export` |

A browser on another machine cannot open the export. A program on the same Seed can.

## Spatial line

`schema` is `spatial.evidence.v1`. `type` is `radar_track_point`. `frame` is `room_enu`. `proof` is `MEASURED` or `SYNTHETIC`. `source_id` is the installed id without a trailing slash. The line is not written to stdout. It goes to the file, or to `GET /spatial`.

No other ADR-384 type is emitted.
pages.glossary:
# Glossary

> Short names used by this cog, with the meaning they have for the LD6004.

**TinyFrame.** The UART framing in the HLK-LD6004 protocol: start byte `0x01`, big-endian header, inverted-XOR checksum, little-endian payload.

**Presence project.** Firmware project codes 0 and 6. Section 6 applies to both. Code 6 has no name in the protocol table. Other project codes are foreign firmware for this cog.

**Cluster id.** The int32 on an `0x0A04` record. When it is >= 0 it becomes the `track` on a `radar_track_point` line. It is not a person identifier.

**dop_idx.** The int32 Doppler index in the same record. The protocol does not state a unit or a scale. The cog stores the integer and does not turn it into a velocity.

**Radar-local.** Metres in the module's axes, measured on the bench with the silkscreen readable: X lateral toward the text, Y toward the bottom edge, Z forward out of the antenna. Height above the radar is `-Y`. The stdout field `frame` is `radar_local`. `above_radar_m` is that height.

**Pose.** Where the radar is mounted in room coordinates, plus yaw, pitch, and `x_sign`. Required before any evidence line. Pitch 0 keeps Z horizontal. `x_sign` is +1 when +X is to the right looking along +Z.

**radar_track_point.** The only `spatial.evidence.v1` type this cog emits. It comes from `0x0A04` only.

**SenML.** RFC 8428 records for module status. `bn` ends with `/`. `proof_` is on every record. Not used for positions or for vital signs.

**proof.** `MEASURED` for frames taken from the UART. `SYNTHETIC` for `--simulate`. Neither one is a claim that hardware has been bench-tested. `CODE` is not used.

**0x0A14.** On this module, the unattended low-power working state, one byte. 0 is low-power, 1 is normal.

**Keep.** The default `--command`. The cog writes zero bytes to the module.

**not_defined.** The report's `vitals` value. Heart rate and breathing rate are outside this protocol.

**Vendor figure.** A number copied from the Hi-Link datasheet or protocol. It is not a measurement made with this cog. Hardware is not yet tested.
pages.mounting:
# Mounting

> The report's x, y, and z are metres in the radar's own axes. They become room coordinates only when a pose is set.

Hold the module so `HLK-LD6004` reads normally and `V1.0` is on the right. Measured on the bench, with the install byte still top (0):

- **Z** is forward, out of the antenna, positive into the room.
- **X** is lateral. Positive X pointed toward the silkscreen text.
- **+Y** points toward the bottom edge of the board. Height above the radar is `above_radar_m = -Y`.

A camera paired with the module sat about a foot above it (`camera_above_radar_m` 0.30). A return at lens height had Y near −0.32 m. The sideways part of that return stays in X. Do not subtract it as a mount gap. The install byte is reported and does not swap these axes. A wall mount at 1.5–2 m was not measured.

Until you pass a pose, stdout positions stay in that radar-local frame (`frame` is `radar_local`).

Room lines require a build with `--features spatial-evidence` and all of:

- `--spatial-out export` or `--spatial-out FILE`
- `--radar-pose x,y,z,yaw_deg,pitch_deg,x_sign` (or five numbers, which sets pitch to 0)
- `--spatial-region region/urth/meso/lab`

Yaw is degrees counter-clockwise from room +x. Pitch is degrees above horizontal. The five-number form sets pitch to 0, which keeps Z horizontal. `x_sign` is `1` when the radar's +X is to its right looking out along +Z, and `-1` when +X is to its left.

No pose produces no evidence line. The report says `spatial` is `no_pose` and gives the reason. A missing region says `no_region`.

A cluster id is the track number on the evidence line when it is zero or positive. A negative cluster id stays in the stdout target list and is skipped for the evidence line. One track is one radar cluster. It is not a person id.

The evidence type is `radar_track_point` only, and only from `0x0A04`. The point cloud is not a track. The Doppler index has no stated unit, so the line has no velocity. The default position uncertainty is 0.3 m. That number is an assumption, not the vendor's accuracy claim. Beam half-angles of 60 degrees are the vendor datasheet's, carried on the line so a later consumer can use them.

Zone flags are occupancy of four configured rectangles. They are not people, and they are not SenML.

Mount the board so the antenna face looks into the room you mean, on a rigid support. A 2D mode in the vendor GUI reports Z as 0. This cog prints the Z the frame contains.
pages.parts:
# Parts

> You need the radar, a common ground, a 3.3 V supply, and a UART that is not the Seed console.

- **HLK-LD6004**, header silkscreen V1.0 on the module drawing in datasheet V1.1. The header pins, in order, are `1 OUT`, `2 TX0`, `3 RX0`, `4 GND`, `5 3V3`.
- **A 3.3 V supply.** The vendor datasheet asks for 3.1 V to 3.5 V, at least 1 A, and ripple at most 50 mV. Those figures are the vendor's. This board has not been measured. The Seed's 3.3 V pin is the right voltage and is not a 1 A supply. Use a separate 3.3 V regulator that can deliver the vendor current, and share ground with the Seed.
- **USB-serial adapter at 3.3 V logic**, or the Seed UART after the owner has freed it. Default device path is `/dev/ttyUSB0`.
- **Jumper wires.** Signal wires only. No 5 V wire.

`OUT` (pin 1) is GPIO P20. The datasheet says it is high when someone is in the region, by default. It is not UART data. Do not connect it to a Seed UART pin.

The datasheet's RX0 description column also says `uart0_txd`, the same words it uses for TX0. Wire by the pin name: TX0 transmits, RX0 receives.

This cog does not use I2C. There is no address and no bus switch.
pages.safety:
# Safety

> This is a presence radar, not a medical device and not a safety interlock.

`medical` in the guide manifest is false. Do not use the output to decide care, fall protection, or access control. A cluster id is not a person. A zone flag is not a count of people. A missing frame is `no_source` or an empty target list, which is not proof that a room is empty.

Do not apply 5 V to the module or to the UART pins. The vendor supply range is 3.1 V to 3.5 V. The vendor also states a current of at least 1 A and ripple at most 50 mV. Those are vendor limits. They have not been measured on this board.

The module radiates at 60 GHz, as the vendor states. Follow the vendor's install limits for a occupied room. This cog adds no extra radio transmission. `--command keep` does not transmit a command. The firmware query is one short UART frame, not a radio setting.

OTA type `0x3000` is not sent. Baud-change commands are not sent. Config writes `0x0201` through `0x0207` are documented in the protocol and are not sent.

`--simulate` and any line marked `SYNTHETIC` are generated bytes. `MEASURED` means the bytes came from this process's UART path. The 2026-10-10 axis check used the UART viewer. This cog binary has not been the process on that port.

Keep the export on loopback. The report can describe where a radar thinks objects are. That stays on the machine that owns the sensor.
pages.sensor:
# The sensor

> HLK-LD6004 speaks its own TinyFrame protocol. Type ids from the LD6002 breath radar do not mean the same thing here.

Hi-Link describes the part in "HLK-LD6004 模组通信协议" (3D presence radar module communication protocol), cover date September 2025, and in the module datasheet V1.1 (size change dated 2026-08-28). The product page is <https://www.hlktech.com/Goods-347.html>. This cog follows those two documents.

The module is a 60 GHz FMCW presence radar. It reports target positions, a point cloud, four zone flags, and its own settings. It streams without a host enable command. A catalog note that this module needs a `0x08` enable belongs to a different Hi-Link part and is not applied here.

## Type ids this cog decodes

| Type | Meaning on the LD6004 |
|---|---|
| `0x0A04` | Target positions: x, y, z in metres, a Doppler index, a cluster id |
| `0x0A08` | Point cloud, same layout. Kept in the report. Not emitted as a track. |
| `0x0A0A` | Four zone words, 1 occupied, 0 empty |
| `0x0A0B` / `0x0A0C` / `0x0A16` | Interference, detection, and dwell rectangles |
| `0x0A0D` | Hold delay, seconds |
| `0x0A0E` | Sensitivity 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high |
| `0x0A0F` | Trigger speed 0 slow, 1 medium, 2 fast |
| `0x0A10` | Z limits, metres |
| `0x0A11` | Install method 0 top, 1 side |
| `0x0A12` | Work mode 0 through 4 |
| `0x0A13` | Unattended sleep time, decoded only as a 4-byte millisecond count |
| `0x0A14` | Unattended low-power working state: 0 low-power, 1 normal |
| `0x0A15` | GPIO mode 0 through 5 |
| `0x0A17` | Dwell life counter |
| `0x0A18` | Output interval, in frames |
| `0xFFFF` | Firmware project and version |

`0x0A14` on this part is the low-power state. A payload that is a float is rejected. `0x0A15` is the GPIO mode. `0x0A16` is the dwell rectangle, and a 4-byte payload is rejected.

Heart rate and breathing rate do not appear in this protocol. The report field `vitals` is the string `not_defined`. They are not written as SenML and they are not attached to a spatial track.

## Firmware project

Section 6 applies to project code 0 and to project code 6. Code 6 is the protocol's own firmware example and the code the bench module returned (version 3.18.0). The name table has no label for 6, so the report leaves `project_name` null and sets `presence_project` true. `--command query-firmware` sends the documented 8-byte `0xFFFF` query once after the port opens. It changes no setting. Any other project code stops presence decoding and clears presence values already stored in that window. Lines already written to a spatial file stay written.

The default is `--command keep`, which does not send the query. Until a status frame is seen, the cog decodes section 6. Run the query once on a real module before trusting the decode.

## Frame rules

A frame is `0x01`, a big-endian id, length, and type, a header checksum, then the little-endian payload and a data checksum when the payload is not empty. The checksum is the inverted XOR of the covered bytes. On a mismatch the cog drops one byte and scans again. A length that would make the whole frame longer than 1024 bytes is rejected. Floats are IEEE-754 little-endian. The worked example `66 66 A2 41` is about 20.3.

Some printed examples in section 6 do not match that checksum. The cog follows the stated algorithm. Those examples are not used as test vectors.

`0x3000` is an OTA command. The cog does not send it and does not act on it. A received frame is counted only.
pages.setup:
# Setup

> Install the cog, then run `--once`. The default command writes nothing to the radar.

The binary is `cog-ld6004-radar`. On a Seed the installed name is `cog-ld6004-radar-arm`. Version 0.1.0 matches `cog.toml`.

```text
cog-ld6004-radar --help
cog-ld6004-radar --once --simulate
cog-ld6004-radar --once --device /dev/ttyUSB0
cog-ld6004-radar --once --command keep
```

`--simulate` does not open the serial port. It feeds two frames copied from the protocol and two frames built with the same checksum function, through the real parser. The report's `source.simulated` is true, `source.verified` is false, and `reasons` includes `simulated`. Spatial lines from that run are `SYNTHETIC`. Simulated output is not the sensor and is not ground truth.

`--once` with a device path that cannot be opened prints one JSON object, `health` `no_source`, null quality, `verified` false, and exits 0. It does not invent a target.

`--command query-firmware` writes the 8-byte identity query once after a successful open. Combine it with a real device, not with `--simulate` (that combination is refused, exit 2). Read the report's `firmware` object. `presence_project` true means project code 0 or 6.

The UART viewer is separate from this cog. From the repository root:

```text
cargo run -p cog-ld6004-scope --bin weft-ld6004-scope -- --port /dev/ttyUSB0
```

On the bench Mac the adapter was `/dev/cu.usbserial-214110`. The viewer can send module commands when you click them. This cog does not. See `MANUAL.md`.

`--source-id` is the id of this installed radar. The default is `ld6004-radar`. SenML `bn` is that id with one trailing slash. It is not a catalog type and not a person.

The export listens on `127.0.0.1:8055` unless `--api-bind` names another loopback port. Any other address is refused. If the port is already taken, the cog says the export is disabled and still prints stdout.

A continuous run is the same command without `--once`. The default window is 1 second (`--interval`).

Building the room-track adapter:

```text
cargo build --release --features spatial-evidence
```

The default build has no spatial flags. Passing `--spatial-out` to that binary exits 2 with empty stdout. With the feature, `--spatial-out` still defaults to off.

This repository does not change the Seed's boot partition, and this page does not sideload firmware. Installing the binary on a Seed is a separate owner step.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Read an HLK-LD6004 3D presence radar on a Cognitum Seed. Positions stay in the radar's own frame until you set a pose.

This guide is for the Hi-Link HLK-LD6004, a 60 GHz presence radar. The `ld6004-radar` cog owns the UART: it finds frame boundaries, checks the checksum, and prints the values the LD6004 protocol defines. It does not report heart rate or breathing rate. Those rates are not in this module's protocol.

The module streams on its own. The default command sends nothing.

The axis convention below was checked on a bench module with the UART viewer on 2026-10-10. This cog binary has not yet been the process on that port. A `--simulate` run is not that check. Vendor current and range figures stay the vendor's.

## The short path

1. **Get the parts.** The module, a USB-serial adapter (or the Seed UART), and a 3.3 V supply that can deliver the vendor's current. See **Parts**.
2. **Wire it.** Module TX0 goes to the host RX. Do not use a 5 V pin. See **Wiring**.
3. **Leave the serial console alone.** `/dev/serial0` on a Seed is the console until the owner frees it. This cog does not change boot configuration. A USB-serial device at `/dev/ttyUSB0` avoids that.
4. **Run one window with no claim that the sensor was read.** `cog-ld6004-radar --once --simulate` prints a labelled simulated line.
5. **Point it at the real device.** `cog-ld6004-radar --once --device /dev/ttyUSB0`
6. **Confirm the firmware project** once, with `--command query-firmware`. Project codes 0 and 6 are the presence protocol this cog decodes. The bench module reported 6. See **Sensor**.

## How the bytes move

```diagram
flow
```

## What you get

| Output | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| One JSON report per interval | stdout | Targets, point cloud, zones, module status. `vitals` is `not_defined`. |
| SenML pack | the next stdout line, and `GET /senml` | Module settings that arrived. Omitted when the window had none. |
| Loopback export | `http://127.0.0.1:8055` | `GET /status`, `/senml`, `/guide`. |
| Room tracks | only with the `spatial-evidence` feature and `--spatial-out` | `radar_track_point` lines. No pose means no line. |

The export is GET only. There is no PUT.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> A missing device is a `no_source` line, exit 0. A bad argument is exit 2 and no JSON.

| What you see | What it means |
|---|---|
| `health` `no_source`, reason `device_error` | The path could not be opened. Check the path, the adapter, and that another process is not holding it. |
| `no_bytes` or `no_valid_frames` | The port opened and no checksum-valid frame arrived in the window. Power-cycle the radar, not only the Seed. Confirm TX0 is on the host RX pin, at 115200. |
| `checksum_errors` / `degraded` | Bytes arrived and the checksum failed. Usually a swapped TX/RX, a wrong baud, or a 5 V level. |
| `foreign_firmware` | A `0xFFFF` reply named a project other than 0 or 6. Presence fields stay empty until a 0 or 6 status arrives. |
| `payload_rejected` | A known type arrived with a length the protocol does not use. The value stays null. |
| `spatial` `no_pose` | `--spatial-out` is set and `--radar-pose` is not. No evidence file is created. |
| Exit 2, empty stdout | Unknown flag, device outside `/dev/`, non-loopback bind, or `--simulate` together with `--command query-firmware`. |
| Export disabled on stderr | `127.0.0.1:8055` is in use. Stdout still works. |

The Seed console owns `/dev/serial0` and `/dev/ttyS0` until that ownership is changed by the owner. A cog pointed at the console device will fail to open it or will see console text, which fails the checksum. Use `/dev/ttyUSB0` or another USB-serial node.

There is no I2C scan for this sensor. `i2cdetect` will not show it.

`0x0A14` in the frame counts is the low-power state, a one-byte value. If you expected a breathing rate, that expectation comes from a different module.

Vendor frame examples that fail the XOR-NOT checksum are not accepted. A silent module can still be a good module that has not been power-cycled after wiring.

The bench check on 2026-10-10 used the UART viewer, not this binary. A green `--simulate` run does not replace that, and it does not replace a Seed run.
pages.wiring:
# Wiring

> Module TX0 goes to Seed pin 10 (RXD). Module RX0 goes to Seed pin 8 (TXD) only if you will send the firmware query. Ground is shared. 5 V stays disconnected.

```diagram
header
```

```diagram
wiring
```

| Module pin | Name | Connect to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | OUT | Leave open. It is a presence GPIO, not UART. |
| 2 | TX0 | Seed pin 10, RXD. This is the wire a read-only cog needs. |
| 3 | RX0 | Seed pin 8, TXD. Only for `--command query-firmware`. |
| 4 | GND | Seed pin 6, GND, and the regulator ground. |
| 5 | 3V3 | A 3.3 V supply, 3.1 V to 3.5 V. See **Parts** for the vendor current. |

Seed pins 2 and 4 are 5 V. Do not connect them to the module or to the signal wires. The Pi's GPIO is not 5 V tolerant.

A read-only run needs module TX0, ground, and power. The host does not have to drive RX0 until you ask for the firmware query.

Cross the data wires. TX on the module is RX on the Seed. Two TX pins tied together will not pass a frame.

The baud in the datasheet is 115200 with no parity. The datasheet does not state the word length or the stop bit. The cog opens 8 data bits and 1 stop bit. That is an assumption, recorded in the ADR. Do not send a baud-change command. The printed baud table includes a value this cog does not treat as a real rate.

`/dev/serial0` on a Seed is the mini UART, and the serial console owns it until the owner changes boot configuration. This cog will not do that. Prefer a USB-serial adapter.

After a wiring change, remove power from the radar itself. Restarting the cog does not reset the module.

The diagram shows Seed pin 1 beside the module's 3V3 pin so the header drawing has a 3.3 V net. If the module draws the vendor's 1 A, power it from the external regulator and keep pin 1 unused. Ground still has to be common.

## ESP32-S3

Use the silkscreen labels **1** and **2** on an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1. Those are GPIO1 and GPIO2, on header J3 at positions 4 and 5. They are not strapping pins on the S3. Header position 1 on that side is GND. Header position 2 is GPIO43, the console TX. Do not put the radar on the console UART (GPIO43 TX / GPIO44 RX).

| ESP32-S3 | Radar | Wire |
|---|---|---|
| GPIO1, silkscreen `1` | TX0 | Radar TX into the ESP RX |
| GPIO2, silkscreen `2` | RX0 | ESP TX into the radar RX |
| GND (J3 position 1, or any GND) | GND | Common ground, including the radar supply |
| Do not use the DevKit 3V3 pins | 3V3 | A separate 3.3 V supply, above 1 A |

Open a UART on GPIO2 as TX and GPIO1 as RX, 115200 8N1. Tie the radar BOOT1 pin to GND before power-up. Leave SWCLK and SWDIO open. Leave OUT open for this UART path.

The DevKit's own 3V3 pins power the ESP module. They are not the radar supply. The radar can draw hundreds of milliamps. Share ground between that supply and the ESP. Keep 5 V off the radar and off the UART wires.

title = "HLK-LD6004 presence radar on a Cognitum Seed"
sensor = "Hi-Link HLK-LD6004 60 GHz 3D presence radar"
cog = "ld6004-radar"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "sensor", "parts", "wiring", "mounting", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api", "safety", "glossary"]

[links]
seed_api = "setup"
